R0058.title: Price Fraud
R0058.definition: An operator uses false or misleading pricing forms or price tactics to deceive or induce consumers or other operators into transactions.
R0058.description: The following pricing behaviors or price tactics are recognized as price fraud: 1. False pricing. 2. Dual pricing. 3. Deceptive pricing. 4. Vague or exaggerated pricing. 5. False discounts. 6. Failure to mark prices on clearance items. 7. Failure to truthfully disclose gift conditions. 8. Hidden price conditions. 9. Fabricated original prices. 10. Failure to honor price commitments. 11. Fabricated comparison prices. 12. Price-quality mismatch. 13. False claims of 'government-set prices'.
R0058.influence: Creates significant compliance risks for the platform and increases the volume of customer complaints.

references.title: CCTV Cracks Down on Medical Aesthetics Black Market in 2025: Will Channel Chaos End in 2026?

observables: Listed original or reference prices are raised shortly before a major promotion, so the campaign price is effectively the everyday price
Store-listed prices do not match the actual checkout price, with hidden additional fees
Fabricated original prices and false discounts show discount rates that contradict the historical price curve
The same product shows two different prices across different entry points, with complaints about price-quality mismatch clustering together
